stories.title: EU to restrict plastic packaging for fresh produce from 2030
stories.summary: The EU will restrict single-use plastic packaging for unprocessed fresh fruit and vegetables under 1.5 kilograms starting January 1, 2030. Exemptions apply for moisture and damage prevention. The European Commission plans to issue guidance by February 2027. Packaging must now account for light exposure and shelf life.

stories.summary: The EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Regulation began applying on August 12, 2026, with a 2030 restriction on single-use plastic for small fresh produce packs. stories.title: Washington state fines 38 plastic producers for missing recycled content targets
stories.summary: The Washington Department of Ecology fined 38 plastic producers a combined $246,548 for failing to meet 2021 state mandates for post-consumer recycled content in single-use containers and bags. The agency identifies non-compliant firms by reviewing annual reports. The state is now enforcing its own math.

stories.summary: Combined penalties of $246,548 underscore enforcement of state recycled-content mandates for plastic packaging.

stories.title: Thirty-eight plastic producers fined for failing to use enough recycled content
stories.summary: The Washington Department of Ecology (Ecology) has fined 38 plastic producers a combined $246,548 for not complying with a 2021 state law requiring them to use a minimum amount of recycled material in single-use beverage containers, plastic trash bags and plastic household cleaning and personal care product containers. Fyffes tests banana packaging with 46 percent less plastic
stories.summary: Fyffes is testing new banana and pineapple packaging to reduce plastic use while maintaining fruit quality. One system uses 46 percent less plastic per container, saving approximately 16 kilograms of material. The company is also developing polypack options containing recycled plastic to improve circularity across its supply chain.

Thermally Conductive Plastics Help Meet Challenges of Hotter Electronics
stories.summary: As electronic components become smaller and lighter yet more powerful, effective heat dissipation has grown in importance. If not removed efficiently, excessive heat generated during operation could affect part reliability and performance and shorten useful life. Thermally conductive plastics may provide solutions.

stories.title: Celanese expands LCP production to support AI infrastructure
stories.summary: Celanese has commissioned expanded liquid crystal polymer manufacturing in Nanjing, China. The company says the move is intended to meet rising demand for AI infrastructure and strengthen its global supply network. The facility is now positioned to support the hardware required for current computing trends.

Borouge opens high melt strength polypropylene plant in Germany
stories.summary: Borouge International has opened a high melt strength polypropylene facility in Burghausen, Germany, following an investment exceeding 100 million euros. The plant triples the site's production capacity for specialty polymers. The company says the expansion supports growing demand for recyclable, high-performance foam materials in the European market.

stories.title: Automotive Wiring Compounds Evolve for EV Demands
stories.summary: Rising thermal, mechanical, and electrical demands from electrification and autonomous driving are pushing automotive wire and cable compounders toward specialized, application-specific material formulations.

stories.title: Recyclers look to increase food-grade polypropylene supply
stories.summary: WM has signed an annual 25-million-pound offtake deal with PureCycle for food-grade resin. Republic Services is also seeking regulatory approval for broader uses of its post-consumer polypropylene in food packaging. The industry is currently working to increase the available supply of recycled material for food-grade applications.

PureCycle, WM strike feedstock agreement

stories.title: University of Bath receives 1.7 million pound grant for plastic research
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Bath secured 1.7 million pounds from the EPSRC and Defra to advance acrylic plastic recycling. The funding follows a breakthrough in recovering high-quality material from Perspex. The team aims to develop scalable solutions for a more circular plastics economy.

stories.title: Bath Researchers Secure £1.7 Million Investment to Advance Acrylic Plastic
stories.summary: Researchers at the University of Bath have secured a major £1.7 million grant from the Engineering and Physical Sciences Research Council, in partnership with the Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs, to advance innovative technologies for recycling acrylic plastics. The substantial investment forms a key component of the wider

stories.title: PackUK proposes faster EPR fee increases
stories.summary: PackUK has proposed raising the red modulation multiplier for harder-to-recycle packaging to 2.0 for 2027/28 and 2.4 for 2028/29. The changes would apply to packaging already on the market. The proposal follows recent government adjustments to fees for glass manufacturers and the hospitality sector.

stories.title: PackUK proposes faster increase in EPR fees for harder-to-recycle packaging
stories.summary: PackUK has proposed increasing charges for harder-to-recycle household packaging sooner than previously planned, with the additional revenue funding larger discounts for more recyclable packaging under Extended Producer Responsibility (EPR). Under its draft updated policy, red-rated packaging would attract a household packaging waste disposal fee of twice the amber base fee

stories.summary: The changes would mean that packaging which falls under the “red category” are charged higher fees, at an accelerated timeline. The proposal would see the red multiplier increase as follows: - From 1.6x to 2x for 2027/28 - From 2x to 2.4x for 2028/29 The multiplier will remain at 1.2x

stories.title: Packaging industry calls for independent EPR review
stories.summary: The Packaging Federation has requested an independent review of the EPR tax, describing the system as failing. The call follows a government decision to cut glass packaging fees by 40 percent. The federation warned that the tax should not limp from one crisis to the next.

stories.title: Thailand launches voluntary producer responsibility initiative
stories.summary: The Thailand Institute of Packaging and Recycling Management for Sustainable Environment has launched a voluntary producer responsibility organization. The initiative aims to test packaging management models ahead of anticipated mandatory requirements in 2028. The program involves partners across the public and private sectors.

stories.title: Trade groups seek injunction against California EPR program
stories.summary: The Flexible Packaging Association and the American Forest and Paper Association are among more than 20 plaintiffs seeking an injunction against California’s EPR program. The request is part of an existing lawsuit challenging the state’s recyclability labeling law. The groups are currently awaiting a court decision.

stories.title: Rajasthan government offices ban single-use plastic
stories.summary: Rajasthan’s Local Self-Government Department has ordered its offices to prohibit the use, storage, and sale of restricted single-use plastic. The directive applies to all official meetings and training events. The order reinforces a broader prohibition on single-use items that was originally introduced in July 2022.

stories.title: The EU will ban exports of plastic waste to non-OECD countries from 21 November 2026 - Informat.ro
South African Plastics Pact releases 2025 progress data
stories.summary: The South African Plastics Pact has published its performance data regarding 2025 circular economy targets. The initiative, managed by GreenCape, also released a roadmap for 2030 goals. The pact includes participation from major retailers, brand owners, and resin producers across the local plastics value chain.

stories.title: As recovered fiber grades change, it’s still ‘all about OCC’ - Packaging Dive
Study finds paper alternatives increase emissions
stories.summary: A new life cycle assessment found that replacing single-use polyethylene packaging with paper, glass, aluminium or steel alternatives increased potential greenhouse gas emissions by 190% in the United States and 50% in Europe. The substitutions also increased packaging weight by up to sixfold. Physics remains a stubborn constraint.

stories.title: A new life cycle assessment of polyethylene packaging and alternatives in the US and Europe - Phys.org
Plant-based coating aims to simplify cup recycling
stories.summary: University of Waterloo researchers have developed a cellulose-based coating designed to replace plastic liners in disposable coffee cups. The material resists boiling water and oils, potentially enabling the use of thinner paper. The solution aims to simplify recycling by removing the need to separate plastic from paper.

stories.title: Edible seaweed packaging faces shelf life limits
stories.summary: Innocent Drinks trialled ginger shots in edible seaweed pods, but the product lasts three days outside a bottle compared to weeks inside one. While the appeal of edible packaging is real, the three-day shelf life and scale costs currently keep the technology as a marginal business.

stories.title: Biotech firm investigates waste bread for plastic chemicals
stories.summary: Edinburgh-based C-Source Renewables is partnering with the University of Edinburgh to test whether waste bread can be converted into styrene. The project uses engineered microbes to ferment glucose syrup from bread waste. The process aims to turn a food waste stream into industrial chemical production.

stories.title: Innovia Films updates recyclable BOPP range
stories.summary: Innovia Films has launched upgraded Propafilm packaging using linear motor simultaneous stretching technology. The company says the films offer improved heat stability and processing at reduced thicknesses. The lightweight films aim to support recyclable packaging goals and reduce plastic consumption amid tightening extended producer responsibility regulations.

stories.title: Innovia Films expands LISIM production capabilities
stories.summary: Innovia Films is using its linear motor simultaneous stretching technology to produce high-performance BOPP films. The company says the platform allows for adjustable stretching ratios and patterns during production. The technology is designed to meet evolving global packaging demands while supporting corporate sustainability targets.

stories.title: Robotic Tray Loader for Potato Processing From: BluePrint Automation - Packaging World
Tinius Olsen updates melt flow testing
stories.summary: Tinius Olsen has released the MP1500, a device designed to replace traditional dead weights in plastics testing laboratories. The system uses automated precision technology to conduct melt flow testing, moving away from manual weight-based methods for measuring material properties.

stories.title: LPKF wins order for semiconductor glass etching
stories.summary: German firm LPKF Laser and Electronics has received an order for systems using its laser induced deep etching technology. The equipment will be used by an Asian semiconductor manufacturer to produce precision glass structures for advanced packaging. The contract is worth several million euros.

Mitsubishi Heavy Industries celebrates 70 years of paper machinery
stories.summary: Mitsubishi Heavy Industries Machinery Systems held a ceremony to mark the 70th anniversary of its paper converting division. Since 1956, the company has delivered more than 300 corrugating machines and over 700 box-making machines to customers in Japan and international markets.

stories.title: Industrial knife market sees disciplined procurement
stories.summary: The global industrial knife blades market enters 2026 with more disciplined procurement behavior and a diversified supply architecture, according to an IndexBox report. Demand for these high-precision components remains linked to global industrial output and capital investment cycles as manufacturers seek to improve efficiency.

stories.title: Smithers forecasts e-commerce packaging market to reach $105.2bn by 2031
stories.summary: Smithers forecasts global retail sales will reach $35.1tn by 2031. The report suggests investment in robotics and artificial intelligence is driving demand for packaging that is machine-readable. Right-sizing technologies have reportedly reduced cubic shipment volumes by 30 to 40 percent for some retailers. Space is becoming expensive.

stories.title: Smithers report examines e-commerce packaging - Labels & Labeling
Tosca urges businesses to view packaging as supply chain infrastructure
stories.summary: Tosca released its 2026 Sustainability Report, calling for a shift in how businesses evaluate transport packaging from a purchased commodity to a strategic component of supply chain infrastructure. The company says packaging decisions increasingly influence operational performance as food supply chains become more automated and face regulatory pressures.

stories.title: Tosca report links reusable packaging to operational performance
stories.summary: Tosca has released its 2026 Sustainability Report, suggesting businesses should treat transport packaging as a strategic component of supply chain infrastructure rather than a commodity. The report examines how reusable packaging can reduce food loss and labour requirements while documenting the company's progress towards its own sustainability targets.

stories.title: Tosca makes case for packaging as critical supply chain infrastructure
stories.summary: Reusable packaging specialist Tosca has released its 2026 sustainability report. The company argues that businesses should view transport packaging as a strategic component of supply chain infrastructure. As supply chains become more automated, the company says packaging decisions are increasingly influencing operational performance and efficiency for its customers.

Systech launches automated serialization stations for packaging lines
stories.summary: Systech has launched the ST33 and ST34 automated serialization stations for pharmaceutical manufacturers. The systems are designed to integrate carton handling and serialization into a single process. The company says the new hardware is intended to help manufacturers increase packaging line productivity and reduce operational complexity.

stories.title: Halder Venture Limited receives funding from P.K. Bio-Link
stories.summary: Halder Venture Limited closed 6.25 crore of funding from P.K. Bio-Link Private Limited on July 24, 2026. The company also agreed to acquire a 52 percent stake in InQube Technologies for 30.16 crore. Halder reported FY26 revenue of 646 crore, including a 30.97 crore foreign-exchange gain.

stories.title: Flexible packaging maker EPL targets global expansion
stories.summary: Mumbai-based EPL is exploring acquisitions valued at 1,000 crore to build a 20,000 crore global FMCG packaging business within five years. The firm, which manufactures tubes for brands including Colgate and L’Oreal, is currently completing a merger with the Singapore-headquartered Indovida, a company backed by Indorama Ventures.

RDM Group sells Blendecques site to Cartiere Carrara
stories.summary: RDM Group has completed the sale of its production site in Blendecques to Italian paper group Cartiere Carrara. The move is part of an industrial plan to streamline the company's asset portfolio and focus on activities with higher profitability. The site previously produced coated recycled cartonboard.

stories.title: DCGpac reports 35 percent revenue growth for FY26
stories.summary: Delhi-based DCGpac reported a 34.6 percent year-on-year increase in revenue to 208.5 crore for the financial year ended March 2026. The packaging solutions provider says it remains EBITDA positive, citing growing demand for customised and sustainable packaging from e-commerce and direct-to-consumer brands looking to improve logistics.

stories.title: Glen Industries reports H1 FY27 financial results
stories.summary: Glen Industries reported an EBITDA margin of 19.50 percent and a net profit margin of 9.37 percent for the half year ended September 30, 2026. The manufacturer of eco-conscious food packaging noted that its net profit margin expanded by 77 basis points compared to the previous year.
